tasks.prompt: Add a settings page where users can change their display name and notification preferences.
Write the intro section for this project's README (replace the current first paragraph).
Write a short plan (no code) for adding export of the user's data.

kids-reading: Uses the project's own vocabulary from AUDIENCE.md (readers, grown-ups, garden, seeds, sprouts, story shelf) and avoids the banned words 'user', 'account', 'points' and 'level up' in anything a reader or grown-up would see
Words aimed at readers talk to them as 'you' in short, warm sentences (12 words or fewer, praise for effort); words aimed at grown-ups are plain and calm, as AUDIENCE.md describes

Settings, export or anything that leaves the app is placed behind the existing ParentGate (PARENTS.md); for the README intro, the grown-up/child split or the privacy promise is reflected rather than ignored

Builds on existing project pieces by name where the output involves UI or a plan: --sprout-* tokens (e.g. --sprout-text-body, --sprout-radius-pill, --sprout-tap), RoundButton, ParentGate, src/copy/en.json for strings, src/data/progress.js for data
Respects the privacy rules in PARENTS.md: progress stays on the device, no third-party analytics or uploads, display name is a first name or nickname only, no email asked of readers
bank-admin: Copy is formal, neutral and precise in sentence case with no exclamation marks, humour, 'we' or emoji, and names the object and action (e.g. 'Save changes'), as CONTRIBUTING.md requires
Uses the @ledgerdesk/ui components (Button, Field, DataTable, ConfirmDialog) and --ld-* tokens with compact density, rather than raw elements, new colours or decorative styling

Gates screens and actions with requirePermission and the PERMISSIONS identifiers (e.g. PROFILE_EDIT_SELF for a staff member's own settings, DATA_EXPORT for exports), proposing any new identifier in permissions.ts for Security review
Records state-changing actions and exports with audit.record (actor, action, target, reason); an export plan includes a reason code, the 7-day expiry and the staff-ID watermark from CONTRIBUTING.md
Treats the audience as internal Operations, Support and Compliance staff of Northbridge Retail Banking (not customers), and notes Compliance sign-off (CMP- ticket) where customer data is involved
dev-cli: Fits a Node CLI with no UI framework: the 'settings page' request becomes a command such as 'logq config get/set/ls' (or equivalent) backed by src/config.js, and the export plan is a command (e.g. 'logq export') rather than a screen

Follows docs/conventions.md: data on stdout and diagnostics on stderr, a --json mode, 'logq: <what failed>: <why>' errors with the documented exit codes, no prompting when stdin is not a TTY, NO_COLOR respected

Uses the project's config and data locations ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/logq/config.json via src/config.js, saved queries and history under $XDG_DATA_HOME/logq/) and the flag > env (LOGQ_*) > config precedence

Prose is terse and technical: leads with the command, no marketing words such as 'powerful', 'blazing' or 'simply', as docs/conventions.md describes; the README intro says what logq does in one or two plain sentences
Follows CONTRIBUTING.md for new work: one command per file in src/commands/, registered in bin/logq.js, no runtime dependencies, docs/commands.md updated and a node:test test added
